title.value: FedShuffle: Recipes for Better Use of Local Work in Federated Learning
title.justification: The paper introduces 'FedShuffle', an algorithm designed to improve Federated Learning (FL) by addressing data imbalance and achieving theoretical convergence guarantees. This is made evident by the focus of the paper and the introduced method named 'FedShuffle'.
title.quote: In this work, we propose a general recipe, FedShuffle, that better utilizes the local updates in FL, especially in this regime encompassing random reshuffling and heterogeneity.

extractions.description: This paper introduces FedShuffle, a novel local update method in Federated Learning designed to address challenges of data imbalance, client sampling, and random reshuffling. The method provides theoretical convergence guarantees and aims to improve upon existing methods like FedAvg and FedNova.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on improving computational methods in Federated Learning, which is primarily a technical advancement not directly linked to eco-responsible initiatives or categories.
primary_category.quote: In this work, we propose a general recipe, FedShuffle, that better utilizes the local updates in FL, especially in this regime encompassing random reshuffling and heterogeneity.

secondary_categories.justification: The proposed method and its applications do not align explicitly with the provided eco-responsible categories. The focus of the paper is more technical and computational.
secondary_categories.quote: Federated learning (FL) aims to train models in a decentralized manner, preserving the privacy of client data by leveraging edge-device computational capabilities.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no direct connection to any eco-responsible sub-categories as the paper is centered on algorithmic and federated learning improvements.
primary_sub_category.quote: Such methods are usually implemented by having clients perform one or more epochs of local training per round, while randomly reshuffling their finite dataset in each epoch.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The improvements in FL do not fall under any specific eco-responsible sub-categories listed, as the focus is on technical efficiencies and learning convergence.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Data imbalance, where clients have different numbers of local training samples, is ubiquitous in FL applications, resulting in different clients performing different numbers of local updates in each round.
